newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends slightly weaker.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends slightly weaker.

text.p: The Philippine peso ended a tad weaker on Thursday at 26.333 from 26.332 after the Central Bank purchased a big amount of dollars, traders said.
Early in the day, the peso had risen to 26.329 in continuation of its gains the past three days after the country's credit rating was upgraded one notch by Standard and Poor's Corp last week.
It also touched a low of 26.34 on a $2.0 million dollar deal which a trader attributed to some requirement for delivery-Monday.
The Central Bank was quoting a bid and offer rate for the dollar at 26.28/26.34, traders said.
It later intervened in the afternoon to buy $82 million at 26.332 and 26.333 due to inflows which traders believe are intended for an investment in National Steel Corp.
"The Central Bank's move was to prevent a sharp appreciation of the peso," a trader said.
Turnover had risen to $222.70 million from $210.10 million.
